clue.text: Flesh I am processing as fertiliser

indicators.note: processing means working raw material over, so these letters are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: A butcher's offcuts, flesh and all, are being turned into garden fertiliser.
explanation.definitionFit: Ground dried fish is a traditional organic manure spread on soil, so it is a kind of fertiliser.

clue.text: Warning article on silly rig

parts.note: golfers shout this word to warn of an incoming ball
an is the indefinite article
daft means silly

explanation.surface: Someone is cautioned about a foolish piece of equipment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rig' looks like a verb or scam; it is the sailing rig with sails along the boat's length.
explanation.definitionFit: A sailing rig with sails set lengthwise along the keel, rather than across it, is named this way.

clue.text: Drove fast (if returning, be quiet!) to find something to eat

parts.note: to smoke is slang for driving at speed, so drove fast gives smoked

indicators.note: returning means the word if is read back to front

parts.note: sh is the interjection telling someone to be quiet

explanation.surface: A speeding driver is told to hush up before stopping for food.
explanation.definitionFit: Kippers and smoked salmon are foods, so this is a general description of an edible item.

clue.text: Doctor taking tea or coffee

parts.note: MO, Medical Officer, is an army doctor
cha is a slang word for tea

explanation.surface: A doctor is deciding between a cup of tea and a coffee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tea or coffee' tempts you to look for a drink in either; tea is wordplay, coffee the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a kind of coffee, originally from the Yemeni port, now often flavoured with chocolate.

clue.text: Fear of arrest

definitions.meaning: anxious dread that something bad will happen
the act of seizing and detaining a suspect

explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both anxious dread and the police capturing a suspect.

clue.text: Armed guard on old car

definitions.meaning: a protective body of armed people accompanying someone
a Ford model popular in Britain from the 1960s to 2000s

explanation.definitionFit: The word means a protective guard and was also the name of a long-running Ford car.

clue.text: What wine merchants might do here?

definitions.text: What wine merchants might do here?

parts.words: What wine merchants might do here?
parts.note: read as two words, a fortified Portuguese wine that a merchant would keep in store; really a town near Manchester

explanation.definitionFit: The clue points at a place, an English town in Greater Manchester, by splitting its name into a wine-trade activity.

clue.text: Monster turns back therefore

indicators.note: turns back means the word for therefore is written in reverse

parts.note: ergo is Latin for therefore

explanation.surface: A monster retreats, and so the story ends.
explanation.definitionFit: A man-eating giant of folklore is a classic fairy-tale monster.

clue.text: The festival season?

parts.note: reads as a holiday period, but points to an old word for a time or church feast that also names the sea's twice-daily rise and fall

explanation.definitionFit: The word anciently meant a period of time, especially a church feast, surviving in names for holy seasons.

clue.text: Copy cure in order to take again

indicators.note: putting letters in order means arranging them afresh, signalling a rearrangement here

explanation.surface: A pharmacist copies a remedy so as to retake the market.
explanation.definitionFit: To occupy a place once more is to take possession of it again.

clue.text: Scorching when clear on hill

indicators.note: on means one piece follows on from the other

parts.note: a tor is a rocky hill, as on Dartmoor
to rid is to clear

explanation.surface: It's blazing hot once you're clear on the hilltop.
explanation.definitionFit: Torrid weather is extremely hot, so it is a synonym for scorching.

clue.text: Composer's unfinished share of mature reflection

indicators.note: unfinished means the composer's name loses its last letter

parts.note: Léo Delibes was a French composer, of Coppélia
a ration is a share

explanation.surface: A composer's incomplete portion of a piece leads to serious thought.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfinished' drops the S from DELIBES to leave DELIBE.
explanation.definitionFit: Careful, unhurried consideration is synonymous with long reflection on a matter.

clue.text: Normal hours worked in the meantime

definitions.text: Normal hours worked in the meantime

parts.words: Normal hours worked in the meantime
parts.note: a standard working week, with a pun on mean meaning average and a week being a span of time

explanation.definitionFit: A typical week's working hours is the mean amount of working time, a pun on mean meaning average.

clue.text: Four in awful terror finding note on something to eat

indicators.note: on means the note is placed after the rest
in means the Roman four goes inside the jumbled letters
awful suggests things in a bad state, so the letters of terror are scrambled

parts.note: IV is four in Roman numerals
ut is the old name for the first note of the scale, now doh

explanation.surface: Four people in dreadful fear find a note pinned to some food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'something to eat' looks vague but is the definition; 'awful' scrambles TERROR as RERTRO and 'in' holds IV within it.
explanation.definitionFit: A freshwater trout is a fish people catch and eat.

clue.text: Vertical kind of paving is completely senseless to a cowboy

parts.note: plumb means exactly vertical, as a plumb line
crazy paving is made of irregular broken slabs

explanation.surface: Upright crazy paving makes no sense to a ranch hand.
explanation.walkthrough: Crazy paving, of irregular stone pieces, is common in British gardens.
explanation.definitionFit: American slang uses plumb as an intensifier meaning utterly, so the phrase means totally mad in cowboy speech.

clue.text: He wrote of French adversary

parts.note: de is French for of
a foe is an adversary

explanation.surface: A writer describes a French enemy.
explanation.definitionFit: Daniel Defoe was the English author of Robinson Crusoe, so he is a man who wrote.

clue.text: Girl in speed crash finds a way to walk

indicators.note: in means the girl's name sits inside the scrambled letters
a crash smashes things up, so the letters of speed are jumbled

parts.note: Lana is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl in a speeding car crash ends up on a seafront walk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'way' is not a method but a path; 'crash' scrambles SPEED into ESPDE, and 'in' puts LANA inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A seaside promenade is a level public path for walking along.

clue.text: Leader in den with no water retired

indicators.note: retired means withdrawn backwards, so the whole sequence is read in reverse

parts.note: a lair is an animal's den
O is nought, nothing
the tide is moving sea water

explanation.surface: A leader in his den, with no water, has gone to bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leader' suggests a chief but means a newspaper's opinion column; 'retired' turns the whole run LAIROTIDE back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: A leading article, setting out a newspaper's opinion, is called a leader in Britain.

clue.text: Try to elicit information on dough that is put on something to eat

definitions.text: that is put on something to eat

indicators.note: on means one piece follows on from the other

parts.note: to fish is to probe for information
paste is a soft dough, as in pastry

explanation.surface: Someone probes for details about dough being spread on food.
explanation.walkthrough: Fish paste is a British sandwich spread.
explanation.definitionFit: This savoury spread is put on bread or toast, so it describes something laid on food.

clue.text: Hour about limit for heating unit

indicators.note: about means one piece goes around the other

parts.note: a term is a limit or end point

explanation.surface: An hour or so is the limit for running the heating.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit of heat equal to 100,000 British thermal units, once used on gas bills.

clue.text: Translation of a Coptic play is outstanding

indicators.note: a translation renders words differently, here signalling the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Rendering an Egyptian Christian drama into English makes a superb play.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally the word describes something momentous or tremendous in scale, hence outstanding.

clue.text: I say! How disgusting a plant!

indicators.note: I say signals the words are heard spoken, not spelt

parts.note: yuck is an exclamation of disgust; the indefinite article, A

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims in revulsion at an ugly plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I say!' looks like an exclamation of surprise but makes YUCK + A sound like the plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A spiky-leaved American shrub often grown as a houseplant.

clue.text: Flower with a double life?

indicators.note: double means the piece is written out twice

parts.note: is, from to be, means to exist or live

explanation.surface: A flower leads a secret double life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' means something that flows: the Thames at Oxford is called the Isis.
explanation.definitionFit: A river is a flower in crossword terms, and this is the name of the Thames as it flows through Oxford.

clue.text: No male person found in the Gulf

parts.note: O is nought, nothing
a man is a male person

explanation.surface: No man is to be found in the Gulf.
explanation.definitionFit: This sultanate lies on the Gulf of Oman and Persian Gulf, so it is a country found there.

clue.text: Missile god put on boat

indicators.note: put on means one piece is placed next to the other

parts.note: SAM is a surface-to-air missile
Pan is the Greek god of the wild

explanation.surface: A missile is mounted on a deity's vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A small flat-bottomed boat of China and the Far East.

clue.text: Secure hold on a tree

parts.note: a cinch is a saddle girth, so a secure grip
taken as written

explanation.surface: Get a firm grip on a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: A South American tree whose bark yields quinine.

clue.text: Poem on child figure's return

parts.note: a son is a child

indicators.note: return means the figure is written backwards

parts.note: ten is a figure

explanation.surface: A poem about a child figure coming home.
explanation.definitionFit: A fourteen-line poem is a classic verse form.

clue.text: Child on track of soldiers

indicators.note: on means one piece follows on from the other

parts.note: an infant is a young child
RY is short for railway, a track

explanation.surface: A child on a track joins a line of soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: Foot soldiers collectively make up the infantry.
